summary: BBN's traffic statistics for the ARPANET hosts for April 1973, as tables of packets output per host. Data for two days was missing. It updates RFC 497 and was itself updated by RFC 522.

plainLanguage.summary: A monthly scoreboard of how many messages each computer on the early network sent.

subtitle: The April 1973 edition of the monthly ARPANET host traffic scoreboard.

tldr.problem: People running and using the early network wanted to keep tracking how much traffic each host generated.
tldr.mechanism: A BBN staff member circulated the same kind of table as RFC 497, this time for April 1973: packets output per host, split into internode and intranode traffic.
tldr.outcome: It is a data report, not a protocol. It updates RFC 497 and was itself updated by RFC 522.

today: RFC 509 is a historical record of one month of traffic. It updates RFC 497 and was itself updated by RFC 522.

sections.title: What the Report Is
sections.content:
RFC 509 is dated 7 May 1973 and has a one-line abstract: the attached Host traffic statistics for April 1973. Like RFC 497, it is a table and defines no protocol.

The table is again headed Host Throughput Summary (Packets Output). It says data is missing for days 1 and 7 of the month.
sections.plainLanguage: It is the same kind of note as last month, with new numbers.

sections.title: How the Table Is Laid Out
sections.content:
The layout matches the March report. Each site has a line per numbered host, with columns for internode packets, intranode packets and the total. Sites with several hosts get a subtotal, the average daily internode figure and the days counted, which is 28 for every listed site.

BELV, ABER and LBL are listed as having no traffic. In March only BELV and LBL had none.

Some printed figures look mistyped. For example, the BBN HOST 1 total is shown as 620150 although its two columns add to more than that. Treat individual cells with care.
sections.plainLanguage: It looks just like the last scoreboard. A few numbers on it seem to have been typed wrong, so check them before trusting them.

sections.title: The Network Totals
sections.content:
The network-wide figures are 66843250 internode packets and 18403070 intranode packets. The daily average is 2387259 internode and 657253 intranode, and the average per node-day is 66313 and 18257.

The packets-to-messages ratio (internode) is 1.06, compared with 1.08 in the March report. The largest single internode count is 11097790, for ISI HOST 1.
sections.plainLanguage: At the bottom, everything is added up again. More notes were passed between schools than the month before.
